newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says invoice value may be used in customs formula.
newsitem.headline: Court says invoice value may be used in customs formula.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday that tax authorities may refer to an invoice price to calculate the customs value of temporary export goods and reimported compensatory products.
Temporary export goods are products sent out from the Community to undergo processing, working or repair, and the compensating products are then reimported into the Community for free circulation.
Duties are owed on the increased value of the product due to processing, under the outward processing relief arrangements regulation.
"Reference to the transaction value of goods is a reasonable means" to determine processing costs under the outward processing relief scheme, the court said.

Wacker Werke of Germany challenged duties imposed on machinery imported from the United States, products which incorporate Werke's petrol engines exported for the express purpose of reimport to the Community. Werke questioned the method used by the German tax authorities for calculating the amount owed, i.e., basing duties on the actual costs paid.

"In calculating the total or partial relief from import duty...the calculation of import duty on the compensatng products must in principle be based on the transaction value of those products," the court said.

The value of the temporary export goods is to be calculated using one of two methods - the difference between the customs value of the compensating products and the processing costs - or adjusting the value of the compensating products by adding to the price actually paid the value of the materials, components parts and similar items incorporated into the imported goods.
Reference for a preliminary ruling from the Bundesfinanzhof in the proceedings pending between

on the interpretation of the second subparagraph of article 13(2) of Council regulation (EEC) No 2473/86 on outward processing relief arrangements and the standard exchange system (OJ 1986 L 212, p. 1)

The second subparagraph of article 13(2) of Council regulation (EEC) No 2473/86 on outward processing relief arrangements and the standard exchange system is not to be interpreted as meaning that a method of determining processing costs may be considered reasonable only if the resulting value of the temporary export goods corresponds approximately to the purchase price paid by the person entitled to outward processing relief or to the manufacturing costs. Reference to the transaction value of the temporary export goods is a reasonable means within the meaning of that provision. Moreover, in determining the processing costs, reference may be made to the purchase price, inclusive of uplifts, of the temporary export goods even if this results in a higher rate of duty for the unprocessed goods than for the compensating products.
